<chapter id="1" level="0">
  <flow>
    <text role="body">
      <fragment page_index="1" source_order="0" bbox="0,0,100,100" fragment_id="0" source_start="0">If  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  is a character modulo q and  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi' </inline_expr>  is a character modulo  <inline_expr kind="\("> q'|q </inline_expr>  such that  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi(n) = \chi'(n) </inline_expr>  for all n coprime to q, we say that  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi' </inline_expr>  induces  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  . A character is primitive ifit is not induced by any character of smaller modulus. Given a character  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  , we write  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi^{*} </inline_expr>  for the (uniquely defined) primitive character inducing  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  . If a character  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi \mod q </inline_expr>  is induced by the trivial character  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi_{T} </inline_expr>  , we say that  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  is principal and write  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi_{0} </inline_expr>  for  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi </inline_expr>  (provided the modulus q is clear from the context). In other words,  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi_{0}(n) = 1 </inline_expr>  when  <inline_expr kind="\("> (n, q) = 1 </inline_expr>  and  <inline_expr kind="\("> \chi_{0}(n) = 0 </inline_expr>  when  <inline_expr kind="\("> (n, q) = 0 </inline_expr>  .</fragment>
    </text>
  </flow>
</chapter>
